name: Sufami Turbo
description: A Bandai add-on for the Super Famicom, released in Japan in 1996, that sits on top of the console and holds two small cartridges. It aimed to make cheaper, faster-to-produce games, and linked carts could share data such as characters between titles.

specs.memory: 128 KB RAM / 64 KB VRAM (host Super Famicom)

curiosities: Only 13 games were released for it.
Nintendo approved the device on condition that Bandai handled all hardware manufacturing itself.
The game in slot A is the one played, while a cartridge in slot B can supply extra data to it.
Its games launched at 3,980 yen, cheaper than typical Super Famicom cartridges.
story: Bandai's SuFami Turbo of 1996 was an adapter for the Super Famicom with two cartridge slots, so games could share data.
It was cheaper to make games for, and SD Gundam and other anime titles came out on it.
Only a few games were released, all in Japan.
